mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over a 3-month window signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 mean excess return) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced household wealth and lower equity demand, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth < -2% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative correlation (p > 0.10) between GDPC1 contraction events and subsequent 60-day S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which erode corporate earnings and depress equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average by more than 3% for four consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12M MA by > 3% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (p > 0.10) between INDPRO contraction events and subsequent 60-day S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both the federal funds rate and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5 percentage point over a 6-month period signals a deflationary easing regime, which increases real discount rates and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both fall > 0.5% over 6 months
failure_condition: No significant negative relationship (p > 0.10) between joint FEDFUNDS-CPIAUCSL declines and subsequent 20-day S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for three consecutive months signals robust housing demand, which correlates with higher consumer confidence and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12M MA by > 10% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant positive correlation (p > 0.10) between HOUST expansion events and subsequent 20-day S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a two-month window indicates a paradoxical labor market where job creation is offset by labor force reclassification, resulting in ambiguous earnings signals and reduced S&P 500 volatility, which maps to flat or slightly negative 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative or show positive skew during PAYEMS/UNRATE paradox events.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year decline in Real Personal Income (proxied by RSAFS) exceeding 1% for six consecutive months signals weakening household purchasing power, which reduces demand for equities and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY growth < -1% for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (p > 0.10) between RSAFS contraction events and subsequent 60-day S&P 500 returns.
